curriculum.lesson_evidence: Audience awareness means viewers can see and hear the intention without shouting or unagreed touching. Projecting is sending a clear speaking voice to the back of the room, with feet planted and the important words easy to catch. Shouting adds volume and often loses the want, because everything sounds like an alarm. Face slightly outward so a viewer can see both faces, and leave space between bodies. Consent means you agree the space and any contact before you start. Passing the loan card can be a mime with a gap between hands. You do not grab an arm, pull a sleeve, or move someone into a pose. If someone says stop, the scene stops. An adult stays nearby for any physical try. The written plan of voice, facing, and space is enough evidence on its own.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Sam needs the librarian and a viewer at the back to hear the book title during the lost-guide scene. Which choice projects that intention safely and without touching?

FEEDBACK
Sam plants both feet, uses a clear speaking voice, and keeps both hands in Sam's own space. The title is easy to hear because the voice is aimed, not because it is a shout. A step of space, agreed first, lets a viewer see both faces. Grabbing a sleeve or yelling the title fails consent or buries the intention, even if the words are correct.

WATCH FOR
Shouting so the back row hears, or touching a partner without asking, is not clear or consented acting. Volume without intention just startles people. Touch without agreement is not a drama skill in this lesson. Repair both by using a speaking voice, an open body, and a gap between hands unless you have a clear yes.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Plan three lines at the school gate about a forgotten note, with voice, space, and the no-touch rule. For each line, say what the character wants the other person to understand, how it will be heard without shouting, and where the hands stay. State that contact needs a yes and that an adult is nearby if anyone performs. Do not use the library card. The written plan is the required evidence.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

WORKED MODEL
Sam plants both feet, aims a clear speaking voice to the back row, and keeps every hand inside Sam's own space. Intention: the librarian, and anyone watching, must hear the title of the blue nature guide. Sam asks, 'Can we stand a step apart for this beat?' and waits for yes. A weaker version shouts the title and catches the librarian's sleeve. It may be loud, but it is not agreed and it buries the intention under noise.
